items.title: Arrival Dock: Lantern Parade Power-Up
items.skillTarget: Given a contextual equal-groups situation with single-digit factors, state the factors, the product, and what each factor counts.
targetSkills: Given a contextual equal-groups situation with single-digit factors, state the factors, the product, and what each factor counts.
items.reuseReason: No catalog instrument holds an assignment-specific frozen contract for equal-groups structure, and instrument:concept-check has zero child evidence and no verified artifact hash, so reuse is not eligible.
items.reviewReason: Published after a non-blocking opening browser smoke check; human child-experience review remains authoritative.
items.mechanic: Each item is one parade scene: equal groups are drawn on screen as real festival objects (wagons of lanterns, packs of snacks, tables of chairs, trays of cups). The child answers by typing a number, tapping a matching equation, or speaking/typing a one-line explanation of what each factor counts. Every correct answer sends a visible amber pulse down a conduit and lights one dock district; the parade physically advances one wagon-length toward the festival gate.
items.theme: Indigo dock interior with brass-and-teal trim per the board spine; every equal group is drawn as a physically countable cluster — lanterns individually visible, never abstracted to dots. Amber light is reserved exclusively for correct power. Large rounded number pad, single-line prompts in a chunky friendly typeface, read-aloud icon always present.

items.title: Arrival Dock: The Sorting Beacon
items.skillTarget: Given several stories using the same pair of numbers, select the one that matches a given multiplication expression and justify why the others are not equal-groups situations.
targetSkills: Given several stories using the same pair of numbers, select the one that matches a given multiplication expression and justify why the others are not equal-groups situations.
items.reuseReason: Discrimination items with matched distractor families do not exist in any registered contract; instrument:concept-check has no frozen assignment contract and zero evidence, so reuse is ineligible.
items.reviewReason: Published after a non-blocking opening browser smoke check; human child-experience review remains authoritative.
items.mechanic: For each item the beacon holds an expression card and three story-pods share the same number pair but different structures (equal groups, adding, sharing). The child taps a pod to feed it in. Matching pods lock in with a beam of amber light to a district; non-matching pods are gently rejected — the beacon holds them up and highlights the story words that broke the match. Two items ask for a short typed or spoken justification, entered on a simple two-tap sentence-builder plus free text.
items.theme: The beacon is a friendly lighthouse-like machine in teal and brass; story-pods are rounded capsules with one-line text plus a small icon-scene so the story is graspable at a glance without heavy reading. Structure-tell words render slightly bolder. Amber remains the exclusive color of correct power; rejected sparks are pale grey-blue.

items.title: Arrival Dock: Fuse Check
items.skillTarget: Retrieve or reliably derive multiplication facts with factors 2 through 9, with accuracy and hesitation recorded separately from structural performance.
targetSkills: Retrieve or reliably derive multiplication facts with factors 2 through 9, with accuracy and hesitation recorded separately from structural performance.
items.reuseReason: instrument:generated-baseline already targets retrieval_practice with numeric entry, which matches a bare-fact probe closely enough that a one-call revision to bind this fact list is cheaper than authoring a new shell; reuse is not eligible because no frozen assignment contract or verified hash exists.
items.reviewReason: Published after a non-blocking opening browser smoke check; human child-experience review remains authoritative.
items.mechanic: Pure, calm fact entry: one fuse at a time, bare prompt, numeric answer, untimed. Each correct product snaps the fuse alight with a satisfying click and slides the next fuse into place. There is deliberately no narrative load here — the contrast with the story-rich nodes is itself the design, honoring the contract's separation of fact fluency from structure.
items.theme: Deliberately quiet screen: charcoal panel, brass fuse sockets, one fact in large friendly numerals at a time, big high-contrast number pad. The side subsystem window is small and secondary so it rewards without distracting. No decorative text.

items.title: Light Wall Wing: The Two-Way Lantern Rack
items.skillTarget: Given a rectangular array, write both multiplication equations it represents and explain what the rows and columns each count.
targetSkills: Given a rectangular array, write both multiplication equations it represents and explain what the rows and columns each count.
engagementHooks: Whether a visual, build-a-grid entry (picture-first) holds this learner through the harder inverse and factor-pair items better than a narrative entry — testing the mixed-learning-style hypothesis with a concrete visual anchor.
items.reuseReason: No registered instrument carries an array-construction response contract bound to this assignment; instrument:visual-explainer is teaching-only and cannot collect item-level equation evidence, so reuse is ineligible.
items.reviewReason: Published after a non-blocking opening browser smoke check; human child-experience review remains authoritative.
items.mechanic: The child reads arrays as physical lantern grids and answers by building equations from drag tiles, typing totals, or explaining row/column roles. The signature move is the double-lighting: after the first equation lights the rack row-by-row (6 sweeps of 8), building the commuted equation re-lights the same rack column-by-column (8 sweeps of 6), proving on screen that both equations describe one object.
items.theme: The rack is the hero: high-contrast unlit charcoal lanterns on indigo, grid lines faint so the child does the structural reading. Row sweeps are amber, column sweeps teal, so the two readings are color-coded consistently across the whole route. Equation builder tiles are chunky, rounded, high-contrast.

items.title: Light Wall Wing: Design the Launch Walls
items.skillTarget: Given a total with several factor pairs within single-digit factors, produce two distinct equal-row arrangements that use the whole total and record the equation for each.
targetSkills: Given a total with several factor pairs within single-digit factors, produce two distinct equal-row arrangements that use the whole total and record the equation for each.
engagementHooks: Whether a visual, build-a-grid entry (picture-first) holds this learner through the harder inverse and factor-pair items better than a narrative entry — testing the mixed-learning-style hypothesis with a concrete visual anchor.
items.reuseReason: Factor-pair construction with whole-total verification has no eligible contract in the catalog; instrument:generated-baseline can log attempts but does not carry a construction state contract for arrays, so it must be authored fresh.
items.reviewReason: Published after a non-blocking opening browser smoke check; human child-experience review remains authoritative.
items.mechanic: Freeform array construction with smart snapping: the child sets a row length by placing lanterns, then can duplicate rows with a stamp handle. A live counter shows lanterns used vs. budget (e.g., 21/24), and an equation strip auto-drafts beneath the build (e.g., '3 × 8 = ?') which the child must complete and sign. Uneven rows physically sag and spark, making 'equal rows using the whole total' a visible engineering constraint, not a rule to remember.
items.theme: Warm drafting-table workshop framing against the indigo plaza; lanterns are chunky draggable orbs with a satisfying snap ring; the live counter and auto-drafting equation strip are large and honest — no hidden state. Sagging uneven rows use rubbery deformation, comic not alarming.

items.title: Market Wing: The Stall-Keepers' Missing Numbers
items.skillTarget: Given a total and one factor — presented either as an equation with an unknown or as an equal-rows sharing story within 48 — determine the missing factor and name the multiplication fact that verifies it.
targetSkills: Given a total and one factor — presented either as an equation with an unknown or as an equal-rows sharing story within 48 — determine the missing factor and name the multiplication fact that verifies it.
engagementHooks: Whether keeping every item inside one continuous market story (narrative-first) lowers switching cost and sustains attention across the inverse band better than the grid-building entry — testing whether text is a hook or a barrier for this learner.
items.reuseReason: No eligible frozen contract exists for paired missing-factor and sharing-story items; all catalog reuse paths are marked ineligible with zero child evidence.
items.reviewReason: Published after a non-blocking opening browser smoke check; human child-experience review remains authoritative.
items.mechanic: Each stall is one item: a keeper states a short problem aloud (text mirrored, tap-to-replay), and the child answers by dialing a number into an equation socket, typing a value, or — on the capstone — assembling the missing-factor equation themselves from socket parts before solving it and naming the verifying fact. Correct sockets close the stall's circuit: lights, music, and smell-wisps all switch on at once, and the keeper begins actually selling to the crowd.
items.theme: Dense cozy night-market palette: indigo dark broken by pools of warm stall light as progress accrues; keepers are expressive animal-adjacent aliens (moth, axolotl, pangolin, heron) with distinct silhouettes, feeding the child's animal interest without leaving the space fiction. Equation panels are brass with satisfying socket geometry; text stays to one or two spoken-and-mirrored lines.

items.title: Market Wing: The Double-Shift Night
items.skillTarget: Given a story where equal groups each contribute a quantity on two occasions, compute the total and show the multiplicative structure used.
targetSkills: Given a story where equal groups each contribute a quantity on two occasions, compute the total and show the multiplicative structure used.
engagementHooks: Whether keeping every item inside one continuous market story (narrative-first) lowers switching cost and sustains attention across the inverse band better than the grid-building entry — testing whether text is a hook or a barrier for this learner.
items.reuseReason: No registered contract covers two-occasion equal-groups stories with a structure-showing construction response; reuse is ineligible everywhere in the catalog.
items.reviewReason: Published after a non-blocking opening browser smoke check; human child-experience review remains authoritative.
items.mechanic: Each item is a supply order for a two-occasion story. The child computes totals on the order-pad, and on structure items builds the delivery plan on a two-panel planning board — MORNING and AFTERNOON panels — by placing equation tiles (4 × 5 = 20 in each panel, then ×2 to the night total, or the combined 4 × 10 = 40 across both). Deliveries then physically run: hover-crates drop the ordered amount at each booth across both shifts, so an under-order is visible as afternoon booths left empty-handed.
items.theme: Warm administrative-cozy: a cluttered supply office window overlooking the lit lane, paper slips with big numerals, the two-sun day-wheel as the persistent visual anchor for 'two occasions'. MORNING panel tinted gold, AFTERNOON tinted violet, so the repeated structure is color-legible everywhere including in the delivery animation.
